lines.text: This is the fastest land animal on Earth, slowed down sixty times.
Watch the spine. It coils and snaps open like a spring, flinging each stride out to about seven meters.
Twice in every stride, all four feet leave the ground.
Its claws never fully retract, so they grip like running spikes. And the long tail works like a rudder.
But now, look at the head. The body is thrashing, yet the head barely moves.
An oversized balance organ in its inner ear keeps its eyes locked on the target.
So even at sixty-one miles an hour, its world stays perfectly still.
